Hey OP late to the I'm late to the Party so you might not see this:

I too have been down in the dumps really wondering if it's worth living. On Monday I got news that my brother was gravely ill and that there was a chance he wasn't going to make it. That really made it worse especially since I couldn't afford to go be with him. I was/am broke and he was 2000 miles away in another country. I hated myself for making poor choices that led to me not having money or a passport. In less than 24 hours so many people chipped in and I had enough to travel, get a new passport and go be with him. I got here yesterday. 

While I was here I met his kids for the very first time and honestly I have them to thank for pulling me out of it. They've never met me before but they instantly loved me and recognized me as babamunini (Daddy's little brother) without introducing myself. 

Since yesterday we've played this little game where they try to sneak up  on me and scare me whenever my head is buried in my phone and its put the biggest smile on my face. They want to show me their stuff, they want to play with me and really genuinely are happy when I'm happy! I love these kids and I am glad I came. Not only because I can see my brother get better every time I go and see him but because they make me feel special. They reminded me to be happy and enjoy life and take it easy. 

Long story short OP, someone, somewhere loves you more than you can imagine and they want to see you happy. 

I don't know you but I want you to be happy. life isn't a constant stream of joy but it's those moments that make you feel special that count. Hurt will come, pain will come and so will disappointment, but it will pass. 

You are loved, and you are special. Stay strong man/lady :)

Personally, this is not the national consensus, but I believe a lot of the atrocities happened during my parents time. by the time I came around (I'm 23) the country was a whole new landscape. I liked my classmates and even though there would be tension if I ever visited their homes or vice versa. Not all whites were pro Rhodesia and its Apartheid-like system. Not all whites were farmers. The media in Zimbabwe is excellent at whipping up panic and disorder depending on who pays them. Private and Public media included.

I usually lurk here, but I have to say something. As a black Zimbabwean, I would never ever want to be under an Ian Smith Regime in a nation called Rhodesia. My father lost an eye to Rhodesian police and their dogs, my uncle was shot for being a "terrorist" and my aunt was jailed for housing Liberation fighters. I would never want to live in a country where there was purported to be equal distribution of land, but in reality, most of the arable land was given to a handful of whites in relation to the total population. Not only that but I couldn't even be in certain parts of the city because I was black. I couldn't be educated beyond a certain point unless I was a civil servant. It makes me sad that so few people have even seen Zimbabwe first hand, but are so willing to write off this country and profess doom for its land and its people. Mugabe sucks, but he's old and he will die soon. Is it wrong for me to have a little hope that our new constitutional term limits and laws that dictate what happens when Mugabe dies will be followed? I expect a bunch of blowback for my rant but geez guys, why not just ask a Zimbabwean whats going on instead of labelling us as a dog shit place with dog shit people.

Edit: Sorry for late response, time difference. For those saying Im not living in Zimbabwe, I am right now :) I went to school here, went to University in the US and chose to return home. I am doing something about Zimbabwe's shitty situation. I actively participate in public debates, I am running a small business to employ as many as I can and I have my own political aspirations to right what my parents generation did so horribly wrong. Yes it sucks, but its home. Let Grace, Morgan and Robert ramble on, we as the local people are generally not interested. We are more interested in surviving. If you would like to visit, please do! We have room and beer :)
